newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks trim losses on bargain-hunting.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks trim losses on bargain-hunting.

text.p: Mexican stocks fell sharply Wednesday but managed to end off their lowest level of the day.
The leading IPC index fell 54.61 points or 1.4 percent to 3,906.25. Trading volume was lackluster at 58.9 million shares. In the broader market, losing issues outpaced advancers by 69 to 16.
The IPC fell as low as 3,895.83 points shortly before the close.
Dealers said the trading had been cautious due to social and political unrest in Mexico.
"The market was listless all day, dealers are on hold. Many are talking about jitters over the EPR," a floor trader said, referring to rebels of the Popular Revolutionary Party (EPR).
Mexican officials said five people were killed on Tuesday in clashes between the army and EPR rebels in the southwestern state of Guerrero.

"Furthermore, the situation with the teachers provides cause for concern," another dealer said. Thousands of teachers have clogged Mexico City traffic in recent days in marches to protest what they consider an inadequate pay package.
Roberto Galvan, an analyst at the Bursametrica consultancy, said increases in primary interest rates and weak trade surplus figures also hit the market.
"The market was on an upward trend that these events interrupted," he said.
Bellwether government bond rates rose about a quarter point to 18.31 percent at Tuesday night's central bank auction.
Traders said telecommunications stock Telmex and financial firm Bancomer led the slide. The two stocks together accounted for 30 percent of all shares traded.
Bancomer stock ended down 13 centavos (1.5 cents) at 2.87 pesos (36 cents) in the wake of primary rate rises that traders said tend to exacerbate past-due loan burdens for banks.
Telmex shares fell 28 centavos (4 cents) to 17.18 pesos ($2.17) on the back of its American Depository Receipts, which declined 1/2 to 43-5/8.
